sam: Heads-up: I'm assembling a focused migration doc for the Optimize toolkit covering batching -> new batch API, KV prefetch patterns, and quant profiles. Want to avoid link/snippet churn in the PR. Can folks spare a quick review?
nina: I can proof the snippets. Do you want both JS and Python KV prefetch examples?
sam: Yes please, short and pragmatic. Also need a compact quant YAML that can drop into snippets/optimize.
liam: Add a tiny rollout recommendation block: canary 10% for 24h, compare quality metrics, and automatic fallback to non-quant on regressions. Keep it a checklist.
marta: Will author the quant YAML. We'll recommend monitoring rouge_l and latency_p95. Also include a note about quant dtype variability across hardware.
sam: Cool. Draft of batch/auth snippet for the migration guide:
```
# v1 (old)
client = Client(api_key=os.getenv('OLD_API'))
out = client.generate(model='redwood-opt-3b', prompt=p, batch_size=16)

# v2 (replacement)
from redwood import RedwoodClient
c = RedwoodClient(token=os.getenv('REDWOOD_TOKEN'))
out = c.text.generate(model='redwood-opt-3b', inputs=[p1, p2, p3], max_tokens=200, batch_hint=8)
```
nina: For KV prefetch: I'll add a one-liner JS example and an async Python snippet. Suggestion: advise tuning prefetch window per median seq-len and cap to 128 items.
liam: Also add observability lines: emit prefetch_hit_rate, prefetch_queue_depth and record which requests used prefetched KV to validate correctness.
link-scan: scan done. Found two internal link issues and one external redirect: /optimize/legacy-quant -> 404, /guides/kv-prefetch -> 404, https://old-cdn.example.com/snippets -> 302. Saved report at /tmp/optkit-link-3487654321.log
marta: Quant profile YAML (minimal; will run tests):
```yaml
quant_profile:
  model: redwood-opt-3b
  dtype: q5_k
  perf_targets:
    latency_p95_ms: 140
    throughput_rps: 35
  metrics_to_track:
    - rouge_l
    - latency_p95_ms
  fallback_policy: "route_to_nonquant"
```
sam: Nice. Add a single sentence under the snippet: "Start conservative with perf_targets and increase aggressiveness after 1-2 eval iterations."
nina: KV prefetch examples: JS one-liner and Python async sketch below:
JS:
```js
// limit window to 64 keys
await prefetch.load(keys, {limit: 64});
```
Python:
```py
# async prefetch window
async def prefetch_keys(keys, limit=64):
    window = keys[:limit]
    await client.kv.prefetch(window)
```
liam: Suggest adding a short paragraph: "Avoid prefetch for ultra short sequences (<24 tokens) since cost > benefit; prefer caching instead."
